Rashi on Nedarim 7a:10:1.hebrew: בנדינא ממך - דמשמע בפירוש "אהא מנודה לך", דהיינו ודאי לכולי עלמא אסור: שמתא אינו כל כך כנידוי:
Rashi on Nedarim 7a:10:1.english: With "I am distanced [nadina] from you" - For it explicitly implies "I shall be distanced [menudeh] from you," which is certainly prohibited according to everyone. [As for "I am excommunicated from you,"] shamta [excommunication] is not so much like nidduy [distancing].

Rashi on Nedarim 7a:1:1.english: Of you - [As the verse states:] “For the Lord your God will surely require it of you” (Deuteronomy 23:22).

Rashi on Nedarim 7a:2:1.hebrew: לנפקותא בעלמא - כלומר, והדין זוז אחר ליהוי לי להוצאה; ודבורא הוא דלא אסקיה, דלא גמר דיבורו דאמר: עלי לנפקותא:
Rashi on Nedarim 7a:2:1.english: Merely for general use - That is to say: “And this other coin shall be for my expenses”; and it was merely speech that he did not complete, as he did not finish his statement to say: “It is for my expenses.”

Rashi on Nedarim 7a:3:1.hebrew: דכתיב בפיך - "כאשר דברת בפיך", וכתיב: "יצא מפי צדקה" (ישעיהו מ״ה:כ״ג):
Rashi on Nedarim 7a:3:1.english: As it is written: “With your mouth” - [As in the verse:] “[...Which] you spoke with your mouth” (Deuteronomy 23:24), [and it is written:] “Righteousness has gone forth from My mouth” (Isaiah 45:23).

Rashi on Nedarim 7a:5:1.hebrew: או דלמא שאני צדקה - להכי אית לה יד, דלא חזיא אלא לעניים. אבל הפקר, דהא נמי אפי' לעשירים חזי — מי אמרת דיש להן יד:
Rashi on Nedarim 7a:5:1.english: Or perhaps charity is different - For this reason it has an intimation, as it is suitable only for the poor. But ownerless property, which is indeed suitable even for the wealthy — do you say that they have an intimation?

Rashi on Nedarim 7a:6:1.hebrew: יש יד לבית הכסא - היכא דלא אמר בפירוש דלהוי בית הכסא, מי הוי הזמנה ואסור להתפלל בו:
Rashi on Nedarim 7a:6:1.english: Is there intimation for a bathroom - Where he did not say explicitly that it should be a bathroom, is it [considered] designation and [thus] forbidden to pray in it?

Rashi on Nedarim 7a:8:1.hebrew: חדא מגו חדא קא מיבעיא ליה - מגו דקא מיבעיא ליה אי זימון מועיל, בעי נמי אי אית ליה יד או לא:
Rashi on Nedarim 7a:8:1.english: He raised one [dilemma] within another - Since he was inquiring whether designation is effective, he also inquired whether it has intimation or not.

Rashi on Nedarim 7a:9:1.hebrew: מנודה אני לך - כלומר, כמנודה שאסור לההנותו, כך אהא אסור ליהנות ממך:
Rashi on Nedarim 7a:9:1.english: I am ostracized from you - That is to say: like an ostracized person whom it is forbidden to benefit, so shall I be forbidden to derive benefit from you.

Rashi on Nedarim 7a:9:2.hebrew: ר׳ עקיבא היה חוכך בזה להחמיר - כאדם שמתחכך אילך ואילך, כך איהו לא בריר ליה שיהא ודאי אסור:
Rashi on Nedarim 7a:9:2.english: Rabbi Akiva was hesitating about this, [inclining] to be stringent - Like a person who rubs back and forth, so too it was not clear to him that it is definitely forbidden.

Rashi on Nedarim 7a:9:3.hebrew: לענין מלקות - שאם עבר, אינו לוקה. כל כך ודאי לא היה מחמיר:
Rashi on Nedarim 7a:9:3.english: With regard to flogging - That if he transgressed [the vow], he is not flogged. He would certainly not be stringent to that extent.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:10:1.hebrew: נדינא מנך כ"ע ל"פ דאסור - פי': משום דל' נע ונד הוא, א"כ מועיל שפיר בלא שאני אוכל לך; ושפיר הוי ידים מוכיחות טפי ממודרני ממך, דאין לספקו בהרחקת ד"א — משום דלשון נדינא לא משמע כלל ל' הרחקה, אלא משמע שאני נע ונד מליהנות ממך:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:10:1.english: "I am distanced [nadeina] from you, everyone agrees that he is prohibited" - Explanation: Because it is an expression of "wandering and roaming" [na va-nad], if so, it is fully effective [even] without [specifying] "that I will not eat of yours"; and it is indeed a clearer intimation [yadayim mokhikhot] than "I am vowed away from you" [mudrani mimmekha], since one cannot doubt it [as meaning merely] distancing [for] four cubits — because the term nadeina does not imply an expression of distancing at all, rather it implies "that I am wandering and roaming [i.e., barred] from deriving benefit from you."

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:10:2.hebrew: משמתנא כ"ע לא פליגי דשרי - דלשון קללה הוא, כמו "מקוללני ממך"; ואפילו את"ל שמנדה עצמו מלעמוד בד' אמותיו, מכ"מ איסור הנאה לא משמע:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:10:2.english: Meshamattena, everyone agrees that it is permitted - For it is an expression of a curse, like "I am cursed from you." And even if you should say that he is excommunicating himself from standing within his four cubits, nevertheless, a prohibition of [deriving] benefit is not implied.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:5:1.hebrew: הפקר היינו צדקה - דסתם מפקיר בשביל שיזכו בה עניים, ומסיק: מ"מ הפקר הוי לעניים ולעשירים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:5:1.english: Ownerless property is charity - For ordinarily one declares property ownerless so that the poor will acquire it, and the Gemara concludes: Nevertheless, ownerless property is for both the poor and the rich.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:5:2.hebrew: ואם תמצא לומר דאין היקש למחצה - וא"ת: שפיר קאמר דאין היקש למחצה, ומאי מיבעיא ליה גבי צדקה? י"ל: דשאני הכא, דסברא הוא שלא לעשות ההיקש אלא לענין "בל תאחר" הכתוב שם; שהרי כמה דברים הכתובים באותו פסוק שחלוקים זה מזה בכמה ענינים, ולא נכתב שם אלא לענין "בל תאחר":
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:5:2.english: "And if you say that there is no partial analogy based on juxtaposition" - And if you say: The Gemara rightly says that there is no partial analogy, and why did it raise a dilemma with regard to charity? One can say: It is different here, for it stands to reason not to apply the analogy except with regard to the matter of "you shall not delay" that is written there; for behold, several things are written in that verse that differ from one another in several matters, and it was written there only with regard to the matter of "you shall not delay".

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:5:3.hebrew: הפקר היינו צדקה - דסתם מפקיר בשביל שיזכו בה עניים, ומסיק: מ"מ הפקר הוי לעניים ולעשירים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:5:3.english: Ownerless property is charity - For typically one who declares property ownerless does so in order that the poor may acquire it; and the Gemara concludes: nevertheless, ownerless property is for both the poor and the wealthy.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:6:1.hebrew: יש יד לבית הכסא - ה"נ לא מספקא ליה דאורייתא, אלא חומרא בעלמא מדרבנן מספקא ליה: אם החמירו לענין לאסור כך לדבר ק"ש; כיון דביה"כ [שאמרו] שאין בו צואה, (אי נמי) כיון דיש זימון כדמסיק, אם כן תאסור ע"י דבור בעלמא כמו אינך הפקר וצדקה, דמ"מ מדרבנן מיבעי ליה, דהא לא איתקש:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:6:1.english: Is there intimation for a bathroom? - Here too, he is not in doubt [regarding a] Biblical [prohibition]; rather, he is in doubt [regarding] a mere Rabbinic stringency: whether they were stringent to prohibit [it] in this way with respect to reciting the Shema. Since a bathroom [that they spoke of] is one in which there is no excrement — (or alternatively) since designation is effective, as [the Gemara] concludes — if so, it should prohibit [reciting the Shema there] through mere speech, just like those other [cases of] ownerless property and charity; for in any case he is asking [whether it applies] Rabbinically, since it was not juxtaposed [to vows in the Torah].

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:7:1.hebrew: מכלל דיש זימון - כאן משמע דאפי בדיבור בעלמא בעיא ליה, דשמא יש זימון; ובשבח מוכח דגם בעשיה מבעיא [דשמא] אין זימון, ומוקי התם בחדתי שבנאו לכך. וכן האמת, והבעיא הויא בין בדבור בין במעשה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:7:1.english: By inference that there is designation - Here it is implied that even with mere speech [Ravina] raises the dilemma, that perhaps designation is effective; whereas in [Tractate] Shabbat it is proven that even with an action he raises the dilemma [that perhaps] designation is not effective, as [the Gemara] there establishes [the case] as referring to new [bathhouses] that one built for that purpose. And indeed that is the truth, and the dilemma applies both to speech and to action.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:7:2.hebrew: הזמינו לבית הכסא הזמינו לבית המרחץ מהו - בשבת (פ"א דף י) פ"ה: ול"ג "למרחץ", דקמייתי התם בעיא דרבינא "הזמינו לבית הכסא", וקאמר התם: "מאי לאו ה"ה למרחץ?". מיהו יש לישבו דגריס ליה הכא: אע"ג דרבינא לא הזכיר בבעיא רק בית הכסא, כדמוכח בשבת, מ"מ התלמוד הזכיר כאן "המרחץ" לפי מה דס"ד התם ה"ה למרחץ:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:7:2.english: If one designated it as a bathroom, [or] if one designated it as a bathhouse, what is [the halakha]? - In Shabbat (Chapter 1, 10a), the commentary [Rashi] explained that we do not read "as a bathhouse" [in Ravina's dilemma], for there [the Gemara] cites Ravina's dilemma [only as], "If one designated it as a bathroom," and [then] says there: "What, is the same not true for a bathhouse?" However, one can reconcile [the text so] that we do read it here: even though Ravina mentioned only a bathroom in his dilemma, as is evident in Shabbat, nevertheless, the Talmud mentioned "the bathhouse" here in accordance with what it initially assumed there, [namely, that] the same is true for a bathhouse.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:8:1.hebrew: חדא מגו חדא קא מיבעיא ליה - מגו דקא מיבעיא ליה אי זימון מועיל, בעי נמי אי אית ליה יד או לא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:8:1.english: [Ravina] raised one dilemma within another - Since he asks whether designation is effective, he also asks whether it has intimation or not.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:8:2.hebrew: תיבעי לך - פי': כמו תיקו, ולשון נדרים משונה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:8:2.english: Let it remain a dilemma for you (tibe'ei lakh) - Explanation: [This is] like teiku [let it stand unresolved], and the terminology of [Tractate] Nedarim is unusual.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:9:1.hebrew: מנודה אני לך - פי' ריצב"א, דלשמואל דאמר גבי "מודרני, מופרשני" דבעי שיאמר עמו "שאני אוכל", ה"ה הכא גבי "מנודה אני לך", דבעי שיאמר עמו "שאיני אוכל לך"; דאל"כ, אמרי' דלמא דלא קיימא בד' אמות דילך קאמר ליה, כמו כי "מרוחקני ממך", דטפי משנינן לישנא ד"מנודה" מלישנא ד"מרוחקני". ול"נ, דא"כ שמואל היה לו להמתין לומר דבריו עד כאן, והוה קאי אכולה מילתא דמתני'. לכ"נ לר"י דהכא ודאי מודה שמואל דלא בעינן "שאני אוכל לך", דאין לספקו בהרחקת ד"א דאמר ליה בלשון נידוי, לפי שאין אדם רגיל להזכיר לשון נידוי על עצמו כשא"ל לחבירו "לא אעמוד בד"א שלך", לפי שגנאי הוא לו להזכיר לשון נידוי לעצמו, אלא אומר בפירוש להרחיק ד"א ממנו. והלכך כיון דאין לספק "מנודה אני לך" בהרחקת ד"א, א"כ ודאי לשון נדר הוא — ר"ל לשון נע ונד ומרוחק מהנאתו — כדמסיק בגמרא שאינו לוקה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:9:1.english: I am ostracized from you - Ritzba explained that according to Shmuel, who said regarding "I am vowed from you" (mudrani) [and] "I am separated from you" (mufrashni) that he must say with it "that which I eat [of yours]," the same applies here regarding "I am ostracized from you," that he must say with it "that I will not eat of yours." For if not, we say perhaps he is saying to him that he will not stand within your four cubits, just like "I am distanced from you" (meruchakani mimekha) — for we interpret the expression of menudeh ("ostracized") even more [readily in that way] than the expression of meruchakani. But this does not seem [correct] to me, for if so, Shmuel should have waited to state his words until here, and it would have applied to the entire matter of the Mishnah. Therefore, it seems to Ri that here Shmuel certainly concedes that we do not require "that I will not eat of yours," because we should not doubt it as meaning keeping away four cubits when he spoke to him in an expression of excommunication (niddui). For a person is not accustomed to mention an expression of excommunication regarding himself when he says to his fellow, "I will not stand within your four cubits," since it is disgraceful for him to mention an expression of excommunication for himself; rather, he says explicitly to keep four cubits away from him. And therefore, since we do not doubt "I am ostracized from you" as meaning keeping away four cubits, if so, it is certainly an expression of a vow — meaning an expression of being "a wanderer and an exile" (na va-nad) and distanced from his benefit — [though] as the Gemara concludes, he is not flogged.

Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:9:2.hebrew: מודה ר"ע וכו' - דא"כ ליתני "ר"ע מחמיר" — תימא: תלמודא דדייק מאריכות הלשון דמילתיה דר"ע, דקתני "חוכך בזה להחמיר", וע"ז הוא אומר שהיה די לומר "ר"ע מחמיר" ולישתוק מ"חוכך". והיא גופה אין להקשות: אמאי אין התלמוד מדקדק משינוי הל' לאסור להחמיר? איכא למימר: אין זה דיוק משינוי ל' כמו מאריכות הל':
Tosafot on Nedarim 7a:9:2.english: Rabbi Akiva concedes, etc. - As, if so, let [the Mishnah] teach: "Rabbi Akiva is stringent" — it is noteworthy [that] the Talmud infers from the lengthiness of the wording of Rabbi Akiva's statement, as [the Mishnah] teaches, "[Rabbi Akiva] was inclined to rule stringently in this matter," and regarding this it says that it would have been sufficient to state "Rabbi Akiva is stringent" and remain silent about "was inclined." And as for that itself, one should not ask: why does the Talmud not infer from the change in wording [from] "prohibited" [to] "to be stringent"? One can say: an inference from a change in wording is not [as compelling] as [an inference] from lengthiness of wording.
